chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara ibn A'yan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, God is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him. Everything upon which the name "thing" falls, other than God, is a created being; and God is the Creator of all things.
Blessed is the One like whom there is nothing, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' [Quran 42:11]

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ: Blessed/Exalted — an honorific for God indicating His transcendence above any limitation
key_terms.خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: Creator of all things — God's exclusive and absolute creative sovereignty
key_terms.خِلْوٌ: Distinct, free from, separate — God is completely unlike and separate from creation
key_terms.مَخْلُوقٌ: Created being — anything that can be named as a 'thing' other than God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about God's distinction from creation in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes God's absolute transcendence (tanzih) over creation. The Imam teaches that God and creation are mutually distinct — God is not immanent within creation nor is creation a manifestation of God. Everything that can be called a 'thing' (shay') is a creature, while God transcends the category of 'thing' altogether. The hadith closes with a direct citation of Quran 42:11, grounding this theological position in scripture. This teaching was crucial in Zurara's time to refute both anthropomorphist (tashbih) and immanentist views about God.
